verdict.summary: OpenWeatherMap does not use OAuth. You sign up, verify your email and copy a static API key. There is no app registration, consent screen or review. The real limits are the key's activation delay (up to about 2 hours) and the call quotas on your plan.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Up to ~2 hours (waiting for the key to activate)

gates.name: Free account + API key
gates.unlocks: You can call the Weather API with your own key once it activates.
limits: Key activates automatically up to ~2 hours after registration
You must verify your email first
Free Weather API tier: 60 calls/minute, 1,000,000 calls/month, no credit card (figures from an older pricing page)
gates.time_to_reach: About 10 minutes of setup, then up to 2 hours for the key to activate

gates.name: Free plan shared across your app's users
gates.unlocks: Your agent can serve other people with your server-side key. There are no per-user allowlists or invites, because there is no per-user authorization.
limits: All traffic counts against one key's quota: 60 calls/min and 1M calls/month on the free Weather API tier
One Call API 3.0: 1,000 free calls/day, but only with a payment card on file. A third-party review reports a default cap of 2,000 calls/day that you can change
Going over the limit returns HTTP 429. A third party reports the key is not suspended right away and you get an email suggesting a subscription
OpenWeather positions free plans for evaluation and development

gates.name: Paid subscription (production volume)

gates.time_to_reach: Minutes (self-serve plan change on the Pricing page)

steps.title: Create an OpenWeather account
steps.detail: Go to home.openweathermap.org/users/sign_up and fill in the Create New Account form. This is a normal user account, not an OAuth app registration: there is no client ID, redirect URI or scope setting.
gotchas: You will not find any OAuth client settings. OpenWeather only issues API keys.

steps.title: Verify your email address
steps.detail: Click the link in the confirmation email. The welcome email with your API key arrives after you verify.

steps.title: Pick the API product and plan
steps.detail: Choose the product you need on the APIs page and a plan on the Pricing page. The free Weather API tier (60 calls/min, 1M calls/month) needs no card. One Call API 3.0 needs a payment card on file, even for its 1,000 free daily calls.
gotchas: The 2.5 API is being retired. Build against 3.0, which needs its own subscription.
A third-party review reports One Call 3.0 has a default cap of 2,000 calls/day. Check this setting in your account so you are not billed unexpectedly.

steps.title: Create a dedicated API key
steps.detail: Open the API keys tab in your account. Create a separate key for this agent so you can rotate it without breaking anything else. At least one key must stay on the account.

steps.title: Wait for the key to activate
steps.detail: New keys activate automatically, up to about 2 hours after registration. Until then, requests made with the key can fail.
gotchas: If the first call fails soon after sign-up, it is usually because the key is not active yet, not because the key is wrong.

steps.title: Run a test request
steps.detail: Send a GET request to a Weather API endpoint with your key in the appid query parameter. Confirm you get a successful JSON response.

steps.title: Store the key as an API-key credential in your integration
steps.detail: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit and no managed auth. Store the key as a secret and attach it to requests yourself, for example in a custom tool that adds appid. Third-party integrations treat it the same way: a key copied from the account.
gotchas: Keep the key server-side. Every end user of your agent shares its quota.

steps.title: Add caching and backoff
steps.detail: Cache responses and back off when you get HTTP 429, so bursts from several users stay under the per-minute limit.

steps.title: Upgrade to a paid plan for production volume
steps.detail: OpenWeather positions free plans for evaluation and development. When real traffic grows, pick a paid plan on the Pricing page. This is self-serve and involves no review.
gotchas: Check current quotas and commercial terms on the live pricing page and terms before launch.

scopes.effect: OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth scopes or OIDC discovery document. Which APIs a key can reach depends on your plan and subscriptions, not on scopes.

blockers.symptom: Requests fail (for example with an invalid-key error) right after sign-up.
blockers.cause: New keys can take up to ~2 hours to activate.
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours, then retry.

blockers.symptom: One Call API 3.0 requests are refused on a free account.
blockers.cause: One Call 3.0 needs a payment card on file, even for the free allowance. The 2.5 API is being retired.
blockers.fix: Add a card and subscribe to One Call 3.0, and set the daily call cap.

blockers.cause: You went over the 60 calls/min or monthly quota.
blockers.fix: Add caching and backoff, or upgrade your plan.

blockers.symptom: No OpenWeatherMap toolkit or managed auth in Composio.
blockers.cause: Composio has no toolkit for OpenWeatherMap, and the provider does not use OAuth.
blockers.fix: Call the API directly with your stored key, for example through a custom tool.

composio.note: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so there is no managed app to start on. OpenWeatherMap uses a static API key (appid), not OAuth, so there is also no OAuth app or redirect URI to register. Create your own free account, copy a key and supply it as an API-key credential, for example in a custom tool. Whether Composio supports a custom API-key connection for this was not verified.
